summary.text: Alexis Rodriguez, a Democratic New York City public elementary school educator, lost the November 3, 2026 election for New York State Senate District 24 to incumbent Andrew Lanza.
According to BallotReady, she worked at Standard & Poor’s and has been a New York City public elementary school educator since 2013.

paragraphs.text: Alexis Rodriguez graduated from St. John Villa Academy in 2006, earned a bachelor's degree in economics from St. John's University in 2009, and received a master's degree in childhood education (mathematics) from Brooklyn College in 2015, according to BallotReady.
BallotReady lists her work at Standard & Poor's from 2007 to 2012 and as an elementary school educator with the New York City Department of Education since 2013.
Rodriguez was the Democratic candidate on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot; the June 23 Democratic primary was canceled.
Her listed priorities included fixing roads and dangerous intersections, fighting rising utility and insurance costs, and securing a Staten Island seat on the MTA Board.
She received 29.3% of the vote to Andrew Lanza's 70.6%, according to unofficial results reported by Ballotpedia and Wikipedia.
